events.title: Crusaders process barefoot around the walls of Jerusalem
events.description: Weakened by thirst and heat, the crusaders fasted and walked barefoot around besieged Jerusalem, ending on the Mount of Olives. A week later their final assault took the city.
events.html: Weakened by thirst and heat, the crusaders fasted and walked barefoot around besieged Jerusalem, ending on the Mount of Olives. A week later their final assault took the city.

events.title: The Byzantines decisively defeat the Hungarians at Sirmium
events.description: The Byzantine army of Manuel I Komnenos, under Andronikos Kontostephanos, decisively defeated the Hungarians near Sirmium, forcing them to sue for peace on Byzantine terms. Byzantium was left in control of Syrmia, Dalmatia and Bosnia for a time.

events.title: Roger of Lauria defeats an Angevin fleet at Malta
events.description: An Aragonese fleet under Roger of Lauria defeated Angevin galleys at the entrance to Malta's Grand Harbour during the War of the Sicilian Vespers. The Angevin fleet had been sent to put down a rebellion on the island.

events.title: Vasco da Gama sails from Lisbon for India
events.description: Vasco da Gama left Lisbon with four ships on a voyage that rounded the Cape of Good Hope and reached Calicut in 1498. The sea route to India launched Portugal's maritime empire in Asia.
events.html: Vasco da Gama left Lisbon with four ships on a voyage that rounded the Cape of Good Hope and reached Calicut in 1498. The sea route to India launched Portugal's maritime empire in Asia.

events.title: Peter the Great crushes the Swedish army at Poltava
events.description: Russian forces destroyed the army of Charles XII at Poltava in Ukraine. The battle ended Sweden's era as a great power and announced Russia as the dominant force in northern Europe.
events.html: Russian forces destroyed the army of Charles XII at Poltava in Ukraine. The battle ended Sweden's era as a great power and announced Russia as the dominant force in northern Europe.

events.title: The Declaration of Independence is first read in public in Philadelphia
events.description: Colonel John Nixon read the Declaration to a crowd in the State House yard, now Independence Square. Tradition holds that the Liberty Bell rang out, though this story dates from the nineteenth century.
events.html: Colonel John Nixon read the Declaration to a crowd in the State House yard, now Independence Square. Tradition holds that the Liberty Bell rang out, though this story dates from the nineteenth century.

events.title: Commodore Perry's 'Black Ships' arrive in Edo Bay
events.description: US Commodore Matthew Perry anchored four warships off Uraga and demanded that Japan open its ports. The visit ended two centuries of restricted contact and set Japan on the path to rapid modernisation.
events.html: US Commodore Matthew Perry anchored four warships off Uraga and demanded that Japan open its ports. The visit ended two centuries of restricted contact and set Japan on the path to rapid modernisation.

events.title: The Wall Street Journal publishes its first issue
events.description: Dow Jones and Company, founded by Charles Dow, Edward Jones and Charles Bergstresser, launched the Wall Street Journal. It became one of the world's most influential financial newspapers.
